chapter: U Street, Jelly Roll Morton, the youth band and the WPA
title: Morton's contempt for Tatum, Ellington and Basie; he hires Malachi to fill in
summary: Malachi hears Morton quarrel with the musicians and dismiss Art Tatum and modern players; because he listens, Morton hires him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Anyway, he sat down and he played for me, and I realized he played the piano very good. But to me it sounded a little old-timey. I didn't really appreciate what he was doing, but the fact that he could play just was enough for me. Later I learned... Later that week I was up there one night, and they were all standing outside, him and some other musicians, and they were into an argument. These guys were... I could see that he was arguing against everybody up there, or everybody up there was arguing against him. But I heard him say something to the effect, "Art Tatum can't play no piano. Art Tatum can't hit the piano with a brick." He really took me back when he said that! But I was listening, and he went on

to say things negatively about Duke Ellington's band, and then he would talk about some band that he had, and name characters in it. Of course, people like Count Basie and Lester Young and people like that, or Teddy Wilson, he just had no kind of respect for at all, you know!

Yet still, I kept my mouth shut. I had nothing to say, because I had nothing to talk about anyway. But at the same time, I would always come up and listen to him. So after... You know, guys just walked away from him. They called him all kinds of "old-time so-and-so's..." I was left standing there with him. So he said to me, "One of these days you're going to be a good pianist, because you listen." Well, I'd been going up there every day just listening to him because he played the piano, and every now and then he'd give me a chance to play. So he told me, "I'll tell you what I'm going to do." He said, "I need somebody up here to play when I'm not playing. So I want you to come up here and play."
